Build guide

How to build the Stair Tree Choir, in order: 14 trees, 4 sites. It is written from the other documents in this repo, which stay the source of truth for dimensions and decisions (CLAUDE.md). Where something is not decided or not yet measured, it says TBC (Rob). The tick-box tests are in test-checklist.md; each stage below says which section to run.

Two safety rules cover the whole project:

  • Mains voltage never goes inside a printed box. The Mean Well PSUs stand outside, beside the site box, each on its own mains lead to an RCD-protected outdoor socket.
  • Never join the +12V of two PSUs.

2 Prepare and check the treads data/blank.json
3 CNC cnc-cutting.md
4 Finish the wood exterior oil
5 Glue the disks, fit the pixels data/tree-layout.json
6 Build the controller board electronics/README.md
7 Boots and pegs feet/README.md
8 Tree box enclosure/README.md
9 Site box and power electronics/site-wiring.md
10 Network router, fixed IPs
11 Provisioning wled/README.md, fpp/README.md

13 On-site setup, take-down, storage

1. Buy and print first

  1. Order from bom.md. The AliExpress order (18 Oct 2026) is due 25 to 31 Oct 2026. The "Still to buy" list has the rest: the Mean Well PSU (one LRS per site), the ESP32-DevKitC-32U boards with antennas, the Pis for two sites, the routers, flex and fasteners. The BOM says to buy 15 or more extra PG9 glands, since the 20 bought are not enough.
  2. Measure the parts the design only assumes. The READMEs list these as unverified, and they may change files before you print or cut 14 of anything:
    • ESP32 board header row spacing (assumed 25.4mm), Mini560 size and pad positions, and that the 5×7cm board is 24×18 holes (electronics/README.md).
    • Board hole positions and ESP32 height in the box, the SP16 socket's hole and nut clearance, the PG7 thread size, RP-SMA bulkhead thread, and the M3 insert hole size (4.0mm) (enclosure/README.md).
    • The outer diameter of the outdoor flex (under 8mm for the glands).
  3. Print one control boot, one plain boot, two pegs, one tree box and lid before printing the rest. PETG, 3 walls, 15% infill. Boots stand upright on the sole with no supports; pegs print head down. The export commands are in feet/README.md and enclosure/README.md, and the STLs are committed.
  4. Print 4 step clamps and 4 washers for the CNC bed, and the pixel disk test strip (fixtures/README.md): PETG, 4 walls, 40% infill for the clamps.
  5. The full print run, once the test fit passes (stage 7): 14 plain boots, 14 control boots, 28 pegs, 14 tree boxes with lids, 92 pixel disks per tree (bore from the test strip, stage 3), and the site boxes (the 6, 4 and 2-tree versions) with lids.

2. Tread preparation

You need 14 treads. Each is a tapered oak board with four old 17mm fixing holes in its back face.

  1. Tape-check each tread against data/blank.json: length about 894mm, wide end about 382mm, narrow end about 92mm, thickness 30mm. These came from photos and are good to about 2 to 3mm. If one is out by more than about 3mm, fix the JSON and run python -m tools.build before cutting. TBC (Rob): the tape check has not been done.
  2. Note each tread's thickness. The boot slot is 30mm plus 1.5mm.
  3. Mark the front and back faces. Find the old holes in the back: two about 33mm from the narrow end and two about 44mm from the wide end, 17mm across and 23mm deep. Check them against the EXISTING layer of the CNC file.
  4. The treads may not be identical, so measure each one rather than trusting the first.

3. CNC

The procedure, layers and feeds are in cnc-cutting.md. In outline:

Each tree is cut in one op, front face up, with no flip and nothing cut from the back (Rob, 25 Oct 2026). Rob does the CAM in NX from the STEP files in cad/ (tools/gen_step.py).

  1. Offcut test first. Print the disk test strip (fixtures/pixel-disk.scad, bores 11.8 to 12.2mm). Cut one Ø19 × 6mm counterbore and a Ø15 clearance hole in an oak offcut and glue a disk in. Check a pixel snaps in and its clips clear the hole. Set hole_dia (the disk bore) and clearance_dia in tools/tree_layout.py and run make all. TBC (Rob): the disk bore and the clip barb flare. These wait on the pixels arriving.
  2. Op 0, once: screw an MDF sheet to the bed and pocket it 4mm deep to the blank's shape. Don't move it again.
  3. Cut a pilot tree first. Op 1: drop the tread into the pocket, face up, and clamp it with the clamps clear of the counterbores. Cut the 92 counterbores, then the clearance holes through into the MDF (helical bore, clear the chips every 6 to 8mm). Watch the first tree all the way through.
  4. Fit a pixel string and a boot to the pilot tree before cutting the other 13.

Safety: eye and ear protection, dust extraction for oak dust, hands clear of the bit. Packed chips are what snap a 4mm bit.

4. Finishing

  1. Sand the front lightly. Do not round the counterbore edges.
  2. Oil with an exterior oil (for example Osmo UV), 2 to 3 coats, including the end grain.
  3. Oil before the disks go in. The pixel fit is in the printed disk, not the wood, so the oil can't close it up; let it cure before gluing. TBC (Rob): the product and cure time.

5. Pixel fitting

Each tree takes one string of 92 pixels. The strings have 100: cut off the surplus 8 and keep them as repair spares.

  1. Identify the data end of the string and the xConnect wires. TBC (Rob): which wire colour is data. Check against the arrows on the string and with a meter before connecting anything.

  2. Fit the pixels in wiring order, which is the node order in data/tree-layout.json:

    Group Nodes
    outline 1 to 59: from node 1 at the base-left corner, along the base, up the right edge, over the apex, down the left edge
    mouth_wide 60 to 68, left to right
    mouth_small 69 to 73, right to left
    lip 74 to 80, left to right
    eye_right 81 to 86, viewer's right, top node first, clockwise
    eye_left 87 to 92, viewer's left, top node first, clockwise

  3. Press in the disks first: one printed PETG disk in each front counterbore, ribbed edge first (front face out), pushed in flush with the face. It's a friction fit on crush ribs (no glue): print the rib test strip (part="test") and the bore test strip (part="bore-test") first and set rib_od and bore.

  4. Push each pixel in from the front, through the disk, until its clips snap behind it. The flange rests on the disk, about 1mm proud. The 30mm body ends level with the back face, so the leads come straight out of the back.

  5. Loop each lead across the back face to the next pixel in the same order.

  6. Node 1 is at the base-left. The string's input lead runs down the back face into the control boot's shelf hole, with its xConnect plug at the end and a loop of slack.

  7. Cut the string after node 92 and seal the cut end.

  8. Test the string (checklist section B) before the tree goes into its boots.

  9. TBC (Rob): how the leads are held on the back face, and that the flange doesn't crack the disk when a pixel is pushed in. Use something rated for outdoor use for the leads.

6. Controller board (14, plus 2 spare)

Follow "Building and testing one board" in electronics/README.md. Every join is in connections.md and the layout is in tree-controller-board.svg. Both are generated by tools/gen_controller.py: change the generator, not the files.

  1. Solder the screw terminals and passives. Leave out the ESP32, U1 and the Mini560 (no sockets: they are soldered in once the 5V rail checks out).
  2. Make the underside joins from connections.md and tick them off.
  3. Check that 12V, 5V and GND are not shorted to each other.
  4. Wire in the Mini560. Feed 12V from the bench supply with a 200mA limit. Check 5.0V (plus or minus 0.1V) at the J2.19 and U1.14 holes before the ESP32 and U1 go in.
  5. Power off. Solder in U1 (notch to the right) and the ESP32 (antenna end left). Current should stay under 150mA at 12V and WLED should join Wi-Fi.
  6. Never power the ESP32 from USB and the Mini560 together. Update WLED over Wi-Fi, or unplug the 12V first.

Run checklist section A for each board.

7. Boots and pegs

Two boots per tree: a plain boot on the right and the control boot on the left (a tower for the box, behind node 1). Details are in feet/README.md.

  1. Test-fit the first pair and two pegs on a real tread before printing 28. Check the tread thickness in the slot, the old hole's diameter and depth (peg 16.6mm, 20mm deep), the hole height above the bottom edge (44mm from the photo), the pilot offset (26.5mm), the pilot hole diameter (the design assumes a 4 × 30 countersunk screw), and that the xConnect plug passes the 16mm shelf hole. TBC (Rob): all of these, and whether 50mm clearance off the ground is enough.
  2. Push the M3 heat-set inserts into the tops of the control boot's four tower posts.
  3. Stand both boots on blocks, so the pixel lead can hang down through the control boot. Lower the tree into them from above, feeding the pixel lead and its plug down through the shelf hole.
  4. From behind, push a peg through each boot's shaft into the old fixing hole. Drive a 4mm wood screw through the peg's tab into the old pilot hole.
  5. Stand the tree where it lives. Nail the toes and heels (8mm × 200mm nails). In the control boot the heel nail is inside the tower, so hammer it before the box goes on.
  6. Thread the pixel lead through the arch into the tower. Bring the 12V flex in through the arch at the bottom of the tower's back wall.

The peg is separate because the tree has to drop into the slot from above; do not glue or screw a peg in before the tree is in.

8. Tree box

L base + wrap-round cover; details in enclosure/README.md. Print the coupon and the seal test before the first box.

  1. Base, on the bench. Push the M3 heat-set insert into the block on the shelf and an M2 insert into each of the four standoffs. Fit the SP16 panel socket (rear nut; the D flat stops it turning), the PG7 gland and the RP-SMA bulkhead in the shelf, all firing down, with the dipole on the bulkhead.
  2. Screw the controller board onto the plate's four standoffs with four M2 × 6 screws, components facing the back. Fit the two Wago 221-413 on the plate below the board.
  3. Wire to the schematic in electronics/README.md: SP16 to the Wagos, Wagos to the Mini560's IN pads and the pixel lead. The pixel current (about 2.3A at full white) goes through the Wagos on 18AWG wire, never through the board. The pixel lead's data wire goes to JD DATA. Plug the U.FL pigtail onto the ESP32. There is no fuse in the box: the 3A fuse is at the site box.
  4. Cord seal. Press the 2.7mm rubber cord into the plate's groove, under every pinch point, from one end over the top to the other. It doesn't need joining.
  5. On the tree. Four 4 × 40 stainless pan-head wood screws with washers through the ear slots and the 10mm spacers into the back of the tree, the shelf level. Plug the run's SP17 plug onto the SP16 underneath and the pixel lead's xConnect onto its tail.
  6. Cover. Hold it with the bottom a few degrees out, lift it over the plate's top edge and drop it so the hook catches behind the plate. Swing the bottom in and fit the one M3 × 10 screw at the lower back corner, until the rim lands on the plate.

9. Site box and power

Each site's PSUs, fuses and runs are in electronics/site-wiring.md, generated from data/sites.json. TBC (Rob): the tree counts per site and every run length are defaults, not confirmed. Edit data/sites.json and run make all when they are. Current defaults: Site A 6 trees (Pi 5), Site B 4 trees (Pi 3), Sites C and D 2 trees each (Pi still to buy).

Mains. One plug lead (3-core 1.0mm² H05RN-F, 13A plug with a 3A fuse) per site, from an RCD-protected outdoor socket into the site box, clamped to the plate and wired to the PSU's input terminals under their printed cover. Mains goes nowhere else in the box. The repo does not specify the socket or who inspects the mains side. TBC (Rob): have the mains side checked by a competent electrician.

The site box is a DRiBOX Large (Rob, 26 Oct 2026). Cables pass through the seals in its lid, so it needs no glands. Its inside tapers towards the floor, with ribs: measure it before printing the plate. The plate is still to design (CLAUDE.md §5); the steps below are the plan.

  1. Fit the PSU (Site A: S-400-12, input switch on 230V, with enclosure/psu-cover.stl held by two M4 × 6 screws) at the top of the plate with air round it, then the terminal cover over its mains side.
  2. Fit the 10-way blade fuse box below it: the PSU's +12V to its input stud; the PSU's 0V to two linked Wago 221-415 beside it. One way per tree run (3A), one for the player (3A), one for the router (2A); every negative to the Wagos.
  3. Fit the Pi and its Mini560 5V buck (Site A: the Pi 3, which needs 2.5A; keep the 5V leads short. A Pi 5 would need 5A, and PSU_MAX_CURRENT=5000 set with rpi-eeprom-config --edit because a plain buck can't do its USB-PD handshake), the PAM8610 (straight off 12V after the player fuse) and the USB sound card. Each speaker gets its own 2-core run from the amp.
  4. Make up each run: 2-core 0.75mm² outdoor flex (good for about 6A) up to about 7m, 1.5mm² beyond, with the SP17 cable plug of an SP16/SP17 2-pin aviation connector on the tree end (screw terminals, no solder; tighten its gland nut on the sheath). Red to +, the same pin every time. Label both ends with the tree number.
  5. Wire each tree box's SP16 socket to its two Wagos with short 0.75mm² tails, red to +, the same pin as the plugs.
  6. Wire each run to its fuse at the site box, lay the cables through the DRiBOX lid seals with the cable guides, and clamp the lid.
  7. Plug each run into its tree. Keep the joints off the ground where water pools (IP67 only when mated).
  8. Stand the box upright with the seals facing down, or screw it to a post or fence.

10. Network

  1. One router per site: a Cudy WR3000 (about £30–40) flashed with vanilla OpenWrt. Set every site up identically, with the same SSID, password and subnet. No Wi-Fi password goes in git.
  2. The show runs on 2.4 GHz only, because the ESP32s are 2.4 GHz. Give it a fixed channel (1, 6 or 11, 20 MHz wide), picking whichever is quietest at the site. The 5 GHz radio isn't used for the show.
  3. Subnet: 192.168.8.x, with the router at 192.168.8.1. OpenWrt starts at 192.168.1.1, so change the LAN address at first set-up.
  4. Fixed addresses: tree NN is stairtree-NN at 192.168.8.(100+NN), the same at every site. Tree 7 is stairtree-07 at 192.168.8.107. Reserve each IP in the router as well as setting it in WLED. Site A is the exception: it runs on the home network, with tree NN reserved at 192.168.0.(220+NN) on the Zyxel OpenWrt and WLED left on DHCP (data/sites.json).
  5. Each router keeps two configs. "Show" is the setup above. "Home" makes it an 802.11s mesh node of Rob's home OpenWrt network for the rest of the year (5 GHz backhaul, home SSID on 2.4 GHz). Save both as sysupgrade -b backups outside git, because they hold the Wi-Fi passwords. Restore "show" before each season.
  6. Not in the site box: inside the DRiBOX the router's 175mm antennas would lie flat over the PSU at ground level. Put it up high with its antennas upright (Site A: indoors at the front window, about 5ft from the trees). Keep each tree's antenna in view of it where possible: 30mm of wet oak costs signal.
  7. Site A: the router stands indoors at the front window, about 5ft from the trees, with its antennas upright, on its own mains adapter. Other sites: in a small covered box mounted high, on the site PSU through its own 2A fuse (the WR3000 takes 12V 1A, the WR3000H 1.5A; check the label and the barrel's polarity). Set "router" in data/sites.json to match.
  8. Connect the Pi to the router by Ethernet: at Site A, outdoor Cat6 from the site box (through its lid seal) to the window.

11. Provisioning

Do this on the bench, before anything goes outside.

Trees (WLED)

For each ESP32, follow "Setting up a tree controller by hand" in wled/README.md:

  1. Flash the plain ESP32 build of WLED (16.0.1 was tested) from install.wled.me.
  2. LED preferences: length 92, data GPIO 16, WS281x, colour order RGB (confirmed at first light on tree 1), brightness limiter on. The limiter assumes 5V pixels, so recheck it for the 12V strings.
  3. Sync interfaces: tick Receive UDP realtime (DDP).
  4. Set the hostname stairtree-NN, the static IP 192.168.8.(100+NN) and the site Wi-Fi.
  5. Label the ESP32 and its box with the tree number.

What M5 will generate. tools/gen_site_config.py (milestone M5, not written yet) is to produce, per tree, a WLED config (hostname, static IP, 92 LEDs, GPIO 16, colour order, realtime on, no Wi-Fi credentials) and, per site, an FPP config (one DDP output per tree, a playlist, and a nightly schedule that stops the show cleanly). Until it exists, do these by hand. The WLED and FPP config schemas are unverified: prefer WLED's /json/cfg backup and restore and FPP's settings backup over writing files.

Players (FPP)

fpp/README.md is a placeholder until M5, so this is TBC (Rob). From the brief: FPP 10.x on a 64-bit Pi image, a high-endurance microSD, the USB sound card as the audio output, and one DDP output per tree to its IP. Each tree's slot decides its start channel and each carries 276 channels:

Slot 1 2 3 4 5 6
Start channel 1 277 553 829 1105 1381

A 2-tree site uses slots 1 and 2, a 4-tree site slots 1 to 4. The slot-to-tree mapping will be in data/sites.json (M5). Upload the .fseq and audio, then build the playlist and schedule from show-night.md (the times there are a proposal).

12. First light and testing

Run test-checklist.md in order; its sections match the stages above. Write the readings in the blanks and keep the sheets. At first light settle:

  • Colour order (solid red, green, blue); WLED is set to RGB (order 1); change it if a tree differs.
  • That node 1 and the wiring order match the xLights model (a test chase).
  • Whether DDP over Wi-Fi is smooth enough for lip-sync with all of a site's trees streaming. If it jitters, the fallback is ESPixelStick in FPP Remote mode, which needs SD-equipped ESP32s, so decide before building all 14 boards.

13. On-site setup, take-down and storage

TBC (Rob): the repo has nothing on this yet, so this is a proposed order, to revise after the first real set-up.

Setting up:

  1. Fix the site box to its post and stand the PSUs beside it.
  2. Stand each tree and nail its boots, with the control boot on the left.
  3. Run each 12V flex to its tree and connect the box.
  4. Mains last: plug the PSUs into the RCD socket and test the RCD. Then power the router, the player, and the trees.
  5. Run checklist sections D and E.

Taking down:

  1. Switch off at the mains and unplug before touching any 12V connection.
  2. Take the boxes off the towers. Pull the nails to free the boots.
  3. Dry everything before packing it.

Storage: dry, trees flat with the pixel leads supported, lids off the boxes with the cord left in its groove, and each tree's flex and box labelled with its number.

Tree box parts: sizes, sources and checks

Generated by python -m tools.gen_components (edit DIMS there, not this file). STEP models: cad/components/ (each part in its own frame) and cad/tree-box-assembly.step (base, cover and parts as fitted, in the box frame of enclosure/tree-box.FCStd).

Status: measured = calipers on Rob's part; datasheet = maker's drawing; photo = scaled from Rob's photo, close but measure it; listing = seller or aggregator; guess = typical value, measure it.

Checks

  • RP-SMA bulkhead: through the shelf, thinned to 3.0mm; it takes 3.2mm at most. OK.
  • SP16 and PG7: the shelf is 3.5mm. PG7 thread is 8mm long (nut 3mm): OK. SP16 thread length past the flange is unknown: measure it.
  • SP16 plug: 63mm below the floor's outer face (plug 60 + flange), plus the cable bend: keep that clear under the box.
  • Clashes (overlap over 1mm³): none.
  • Board stack: the ESP32's tallest part reaches y = 21.4mm; the cover's back wall is at y = 47, so 25.6mm spare.
  • Mini560 standing on the board: its top end reaches y = 44.6mm, 2.4mm short of the back wall. Clear of the ESP32 by 5.5mm (column A is at the box's high-x side).
  • ESP32 USB end reaches x = 11.8mm; the cover's inside wall is at x = -0.25.

← Bill of materialsCutting a tree on the CNC →

Cutting a tree on the CNC

One tree per setup, in one op, front face up, no flip (Rob, 25 Oct 2026). Nothing is cut from the back: the pixel leads loop across the back face. Not a production run: take it gently and watch the first one all the way through.

Rob does the CAM in Siemens NX from the STEP files made by tools/gen_step.py (needs requirements-cad.txt; python -m tools.build skips it without CadQuery):

File What
cad/stair-tree.step the finished tread: rounded 18mm corners, 92 counterbores and clearance holes, the old fixing holes in the back
cad/fixture-plate.step MDF plate (18mm default), blank bounding box + 50mm all round, with a 4mm pocket the shape of the blank
cad/stair-tree-assembly.step the two together, tree sitting in the pocket

For assembling the rest in NX, tools/gen_printed.py (OpenSCAD + CadQuery) makes the printed parts STEP solids in cad/printed/ (boots, pegs, PSU cover, step clamp and washer, pixel disk), each as fitted, and cad/stair-tree-kit.step: the tree with both boots, pegs and 92 pixel disks in place (the tree box isn't placed yet), in the same axes as cad/stair-tree.step. They are made from the OpenSCAD meshes, so flat faces are planes and curved ones are faceted. The tree box's own STEPs come from FreeCAD and have real surfaces (tools/tree_box_export.py). The frames are listed at the top of the tool.

Axes: mm, Z up, the tree's front face at Z = 0 (the part runs from Z = −30 to 0), X right, Y up (the tree's top is +Y), origin at the bottom-left of the blank's bounding box. The plate shares the origin, so its top is at Z = −26. The pocket is drawn at zero clearance: set the offset in CAM.

The 2D file stays as reference: cad/stair-tree-cnc-layout.svg (python -m tools.gen_cnc also writes a .dxf, not committed), mm, front view. Layers:

Layer Op What
FRONT_COUNTERBORE 1 92 × Ø19 × 6mm, for the printed pixel disks
FRONT_HOLES 1 92 × Ø15 clearance holes, right through
EXISTING — reference only: the old fixing holes in the back (not mirrored). Don't cut.
BLANK — the tread outline, for positioning only

How the pixel sits: a printed PETG disk (fixtures/pixel-disk.scad, a 2mm front lip with bore hole_dia) is pressed into the counterbore on crush ribs (after varnish the counterbores measured 18.3–18.6 × 4.9, so the disk is 4.8 thick); the bullet pushes in from the front, its Ø13.6 flange resting on the disk and its clips snapping behind the lip. The fit is set by the printed bore, not the oak.

Before the first tree

  1. Offcut test (pixels needed): print the disk test strip (bores 11.8 to 12.2), and cut one Ø19 × 6 counterbore and Ø15 clearance hole in an oak offcut. Glue a disk in, and check a pixel snaps in and its clips clear the hole. Set hole_dia (disk bore) and clearance_dia in tools/tree_layout.py, then make all. TBC (Rob): the clip barb flare, which sets clearance_dia.
  2. Tape-check the tread against data/blank.json: length ~894, wide end ~382, narrow end ~92. If one is out by more than about 3mm, fix the JSON and regenerate before cutting.

Op 0: fixture pocket (once)

  • Screw an MDF sheet (18mm, or set plate_thickness in tools/gen_step.py) to the bed, at least the blank plus 50mm all round.
  • Pocket it 4mm deep to the blank outline, with your clearance offset. Rob may use a bigger bit than the 4mm for this.
  • Drop a tread in to check the fit before cutting any tree.
  • Never move the plate again. XY zero stays where it is for every tree.

Op 1: front face up, counterbores and holes

  • Drop the tread into the pocket, front face up, narrow end towards +Y. Hold it down with workshop clamps (or the printed step clamps, fixtures/, with spoil_t set to the plate less the pocket: 14mm for 18mm MDF). The pocket locates it; the clamps only stop it lifting.
  • Clamp clearance: the counterbore edge is ~12.5mm in from the blank edge, so grip no more than 10mm of the edge, between pixels where you can. Check every clamp against the toolpath before starting.
  • Z zero on the tread's front face; touch off each tree, as the thickness varies.
  • Counterbores: Ø19 × 6mm (Rob, after the first-off run, 26 Oct 2026), to the finished size (the disk's crush ribs take up what varnish leaves, 18.3–18.6 measured).
  • Clearance holes: helical bore Ø15 through, to 0.5mm into the MDF. Holes through the pocket floor are fine; each tree reuses the same spots.
  • Peck/clear: lift out of the hole every 6–8mm of depth and blow the chips out. Deep oak holes pack with chips, and packed chips are what snap a 4mm bit.

Feeds for oak (starting point, 4mm 2-flute carbide)

4mm two-flute carbide end mill with enough reach for 30mm (Rob, 23 Oct 2026). Rob may choose other tools in NX.

Value
Spindle 18,000 rpm
Feed 800–1000 mm/min (≈0.025mm per tooth: gentle)
Plunge / helix 300 mm/min, helix step 1mm per turn
Depth per pass 1mm per helix turn in the holes; the counterbore in 1mm steps
Width per pass ≤ 40% of the bit in the counterbore; or adaptive clearing
Finish a 0.2mm finishing pass on the counterbore wall, so the disk drops in

Listen and look at the chips: dust means the feed is too slow (heat dulls the bit); a screech or shower of splinters means it's too fast or too deep. Slow down in the narrow top end, where there's less wood to hold the board.

After cutting

Sand the front lightly (don't round the counterbore edges), then oil per CLAUDE.md §3. Glue the disks in after the oil has cured (build-guide §5); the fit is in the disk, so the oil can't close it up.

  • Pi supply at its input: ____ V (at least 4.9V under load; no under-voltage warning in FPP's status)
  • FPP has one DDP output per tree: right IP, start channel of its slot, 276 channels
  • Slot-to-tree mapping matches data/sites.json
  • USB sound card selected as the FPP audio output
  • Audio test plays through the PAM8610 and both speakers (left and right) with no hum or crackle
  • Volume set for the site: ____ (a quieter level after 20:00 is proposed in show-night.md)
  • PAM8610 is not hot after 10 minutes

E. Show

  • The sequence plays from FPP (not from the PC), with audio
  • Every tree uses all four mouth shapes and rests on the lip in instrumentals
  • Eyes blink
  • Only the trees arranged to sing move their mouths
  • The Waiting loop plays and its one-minute pieces follow each other without a flicker (show-night.md "The silent loops")
  • Schedule starts the show: set ____ (16:00 is proposed), started ____
  • After the Goodnight the Night loop starts by itself, dim, with no dark gap
  • Lights out from Home Assistant: the scene playing finishes, Lights Out plays, the trees go dark and stay dark; time from lights out to dark ____ (at most ~1 min 20 s)
  • Backstop: with no lights out, the Night loop stops gracefully at 23:30 and the trees are dark by 23:32
  • Morning: HA starts it at the alarm; lights out stops it the same way (Morning Lights Off, then dark)
  • After a power cut, the player and trees come back and the schedule carries on. TBC (Rob): nothing in the repo says whether FPP is set to resume.
  • One whole evening runs without a dropout or anything overheating
  • Spares are on site: fuses, an ESP32, a 74AHCT125, a Mini560, spare pixels

Show night

Draft, 23 Oct 2026. Everything here plays from the site's FPP player on a schedule; Home Assistant (M7) can later start it at sunset or hold it when nobody's home. Times are a proposal for Rob to change.

Running order

UK sunset in December is about 15:50.

Time What plays Sound
16:00 Waiting loop (10 minutes, ten one-minute scenes): the choir mucking about between shows, a different background in every scene. Mexican waves, Noel showing off, a game of catch, Bramble nodding off, Ivy copying Holly, Jingle fidgeting, watching passers-by (below) none
every :15, :30, :45, 16:15 to 19:45 Announcement (~13 s): "Next show at five o'clock!" (the 19:xx ones announce the last show, at eight) the trees, lip-synced
17:00, 18:00, 19:00, 20:00 (last) Show (~15 min), then back to the waiting loop full
21:00 Goodnight skit; the trees settle into a dim, sleepy breath the trees
after the Goodnight Night loop: the trees doze, yawn, peek and giggle, dim and slow, until lights out none
lights out Home Assistant stops the Night loop gracefully when the living room lights go off: the scene playing finishes, then Lights Out (20 s: last yawns, Holly shushes, eyes close, the trees go dark one by one). FPP's backstop: the Night loop's window closes at 23:30 with the same graceful stop. none

Specials (Saturday Special at 18:00 on December Saturdays, New Year's Eve to the midnight countdown, New Year's Day 15:00–19:00): specials.md.

Volume: a "quiet hours" level after 20:00 if the neighbours ask. FPP's scheduler runs this; the playlists are generated per site (M5) so every site gets the same shows.

A show (~15 minutes)

Four songs plus short skits between them. Three set lists rotate through the evening so people who stay see something new.

Set A (17:00, 20:00) Set B (18:00) Set C (19:00)
Opening skit Tuning up Tuning up Tuning up
1 Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree Feliz Navidad We Wish You a Merry Christmas
skit Who's singing next? Pip's joke Bramble falls asleep
2 Dominick the Donkey Frosty the Snowman Twelve Days of Christmas (Bramble asleep)
skit Bramble falls asleep Who's singing next? Bramble wakes up
3 Little Drummer Boy (Bramble asleep) O Come All Ye Faithful The Virgin Mary Had a Baby Boy
skit Bramble wakes up
4 We Wish You a Merry Christmas Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree Dominick the Donkey
Closing Thank you / next show Thank you / next show Thank you / next show

Bramble's story (24 Oct 2026) is complete in Sets A and C: he nods off, sleeps through the next song (eyes shut, outline a slow dim blue breath, the others cover his lines; Twelve Days' fifth day goes to Jingle and Pip either side of him), and Holly wakes him after it. Little Drummer Boy and Twelve Days have him asleep throughout, so they may only follow "Bramble falls asleep" (a test checks the set lists).

Between the pieces: 3–5 s of the waiting look so the songs don't run into each other.

The choir

Six characters, one per sequence slot (left to right as you face them), so every site gets the same cast whichever physical trees it has. Names and voices are proposals. Their backstories, name-tag lines and answers for curious visitors: backstory.md.

Slot Name Character Voice (ElevenLabs, 24 Oct 2026) Piper fallback
1 Holly The conductor. Bossy, counts everyone in. Alice (British, clear) en_GB, female, crisp
2 Ivy Holly's sidekick, agrees with everything. Lily (British, warm) en_GB, female, bright, pitched up
3 Noel The show-off tenor. Holds every note too long. Eric (smooth tenor) en_GB, male, pitched down
4 Jingle Over-excited. Talks fast. Liam (energetic, fastest) en_GB, male, pitched up
5 Bramble Sleepy. Nods off between songs. Bill (old, lowest, slowest) en_GB, male, slow, low
6 Pip The smallest voice. Tells terrible jokes. Laura (quirky) en_GB, female, high

Voices: ElevenLabs premade voices with the eleven_v3 model, directed per line with audio tags ([sleepily], [giggles]) in the scripts; tools/skit.py caches every clip, so re-runs are free. Picked by Claude from measured pitch and pace without listening, so they're proposals: auditions of three candidates per character are in the show folder's Audio\Skits\auditions\. To change one, set its voice id in data/voices.json and re-run the skits. Piper (--engine piper) stays as the free, offline fallback. Lip-sync uses the same lyric-timing tools as the songs, kept inside each line's known span of audio.

Scripts (first drafts)

Eyes in brackets: the eye moves from tools/fx.py.

Announcement (every quarter hour, one per show time)

Holly: Hello everyone! We're the Stair Tree Choir!
Jingle: And our next show starts at five o'clock!
Pip: Bring your friends! And your grandma! And your grandma's friends!
Holly: See you then! (all: eyes roll)

Tuning up (opening)

Holly: Places, everyone! Places!
Noel: Mi-mi-mi-mi-miiiiiiiii… (Noel's eyes: rainbow)
Holly: Thank you, Noel.
Noel: …miiiiiiiiiiiii—
Holly: THANK you, Noel. (everyone looks at Noel)
Holly: Bramble? … Bramble!
Bramble: (eyes open) I'm awake! I'm awake!
Holly: One, two, three, four!

Who's singing next?

Jingle: Ooh, ooh, can I sing the next one? Can I? Can I?
Holly: Everyone sings the next one, Jingle.
Jingle: Even me?!
Ivy: Especially you.

Pip's joke

Pip: What do you call a tree that's afraid of Christmas?
Ivy: I don't know, Pip, what?
Pip: A fir-aid-y cat!
(everyone looks at Pip; long pause; Noel's eyes roll)
Holly: …Next song.

Bramble falls asleep / wakes up

Bramble: (yawns) Is it nearly the end?
Holly: It's the second song, Bramble.
Bramble: zzzz… (Bramble's eyes close; snoring)
(later) Holly: BRAMBLE! Bramble: Present!

Thank you / next show

Holly: Thank you for listening! We've been the Stair Tree Choir!
Pip: Our next show is at six o'clock!
Everyone: Merry Christmas!

Goodnight (21:00)

Holly: That's all for tonight, everyone.
Bramble: Finally… (eyes close)
Pip: Goodnight! Sleep tight! Don't let the reindeer bite!
Everyone: Goodniiiight! (they settle one by one, Noel last after his long note: heavy eyes, a dim warm breath; Bramble's already asleep. That's where the Night loop picks up.)

The silent loops

Built 25 Oct 2026 (tools/loops.py, arrangements in data/loops/). No audio. Each loop is a run of short sequences, one scene each, played in order by its FPP playlist and repeated; short so that a graceful stop (lights out) only waits for the end of the scene that's playing. Each playlist has a lead-out that FPP plays after a graceful stop and then goes idle; a hard stop (a show cutting in) skips it. The characters act through eyes (look at each other, roll, wink, heavy lids, close), outline looks of their own (glow, breathe, bounce, swell, sparkle, a ball of light running round) and mouth shapes (yawn, silent hum, giggle, chatter, whisper, snore, shush); otherwise mouths rest on the lip. Nothing strobes; the quickest thing is Jingle's bounce on his own tree. Character colours: Holly red, Ivy green, Noel gold, Jingle orange, Bramble blue, Pip pink.

Playlist Pieces Lead-out When
Waiting Waiting 1-10, 60 s each (10 min) Lights Out 16:00 to the Goodnight, scheduled; shows cut in with a hard stop
Waiting Asleep Waiting Asleep 1-10: the same scenes with Bramble asleep throughout (the others still nudge him; he sleeps on) Lights Out New Year's Eve, from Bramble nodding off (23:20) to the countdown
Night Night 1-8, 50 s each (6:40), brightness 45 % Lights Out (20 s, ends black) after the 21:00 Goodnight until lights out, backstop 23:30; also 00:00-00:30 on New Year's Day, after the countdown
Night Christmas Eve Night Christmas Eve 1-3, 40 s each: all asleep for Santa, only the gentlest stirring Lights Out Asleep (12 s, the sleepers fade out one by one) Christmas Eve after the Goodnight, backstop 23:30
Morning Morning 1-6, 45 s each, brightness 85 % Morning Lights Off (15 s: a goodbye wave, a wink each, off one by one) not scheduled: Home Assistant starts it with Rob's alarm and stops it at the morning lights out (sunrise + 90 min). Backstop: repeat off and the six pieces listed 40 times (3 hours), so it ends by itself through its lead-out

Every scene, with its background look:

Piece Length Background What happens
Waiting 1 60 s rainbow wash Mexican wave: down the line, back in everyone's own colour, then faster; Bramble is late
Waiting 2 60 s choir butterfly Noel shows off with a rainbow shimmer; the others roll their eyes; Holly stops him; he tries again
Waiting 3 60 s breathing rainbow Pass the ball: Pip and Jingle throw a ball of light over Bramble, up to Holly, who throws it back; Pip drops it
Waiting 4 60 s spirals Bramble nods off; Ivy tells Holly; Holly's nudge runs down the line and he wakes with a start
Waiting 5 60 s marquee Ivy copies everything Holly does, a beat behind; Holly notices; Pip joins in
Waiting 6 60 s plasma Jingle can't keep still: bouncing, eyes rolling, chattering; Holly shushes him; Pip joins in
Waiting 7 60 s rainbow sweep, then breathing Passers-by: the trees watch someone walk past, show off to them, pose; a silent hum to finish
Waiting 8 60 s breathing rainbow The silent hum: Holly conducts, Noel holds the last note far too long, Holly stops him, he bows
Waiting 9 60 s a colour each, then icy spirals Colour relay: every tree passes its colour to its neighbour; Pip muddles it; then the ball goes round everyone
Waiting 10 60 s icy spirals, then fire Snow: everyone looks up in wonder; Jingle's delighted; Pip catches a snowflake; then cosy by the fire
Night 1 50 s warm breath Settling down: yawns go round, Bramble's already snoring, Jingle's wide awake until Holly shushes him
Night 2 50 s blue breath Can't sleep: Jingle peeks, whispers to Pip, Pip whispers back; Holly shushes; Jingle peeks again
Night 3 50 s low fire Doze and poke: Noel nods off, Jingle pokes him and pretends to be asleep; later Pip does it too
Night 4 50 s purple breath Snore glow: Bramble snores, his glow swelling with every snore; Ivy rolls her eyes; Holly's nudge travels down the line
Night 5 50 s teal breath Giggles: Pip and Jingle set each other off, a sparkle passing between them over sleeping Bramble; Holly shushes
Night 6 50 s navy breath Peekaboo: they take turns to peek; Pip and Holly peek at each other at the same moment; Bramble talks in his sleep
Night 7 50 s slow icy spiral Noel's dream: asleep, he glitters gold and silently sings his solo; Holly rolls her eyes
Night 8 50 s slow blue breath down the line Deep sleep: slow breaths roll down the line, soft snores; Holly checks everyone's asleep
Night Christmas Eve 1-3 40 s everyone's sleeping breath Pip peeks to see if Santa's been; Jingle giggles in a dream; Ivy hums in her sleep; Noel dreams in gold; Holly checks; Jingle looks up for the sleigh; Bramble snores
Morning 1 45 s pink breath Waking up: Jingle's been awake for ages; eyes open one by one with yawns and stretches; Bramble snores on
Morning 2 45 s gold breath Holly's roll call: she looks at each tree in turn and they answer with a blink and a colour pop; Jingle answers too early, Noel shows off, Bramble doesn't answer at all
Morning 3 45 s sunrise spirals Bramble won't wake: Holly and Ivy nudge him, then Pip and Jingle from the other side; he opens one eye, and shuts it again
Morning 4 45 s rainbow wash Pip's sunrise: a sparkle on Pip spreads up the line in gold and everyone looks up; then Noel warms up, silently
Morning 5 45 s daylight marquee Off to work and school: the trees watch people go past, Jingle bounces at them, everyone stretches up in daylight
Morning 6 45 s breathing rainbow Ready for the day: everyone hums; Bramble finally wakes properly and the others cheer with a gold wave

Lights out comes from Home Assistant (Rob's HA repo): in the evening when the living room lights go off, in the morning at sunrise + 90 min; it stops the playlist gracefully (ALLPLAYLISTS or the playlist by name). FPP doesn't restart a playlist stopped by hand in the same schedule window (Scheduler.cpp, "just force stopped"), so the trees stay dark. If HA never says, the Night loop's schedule window ends at 23:30 (00:30 on New Year's night) with a graceful stop: dark by about 23:31:30 at the latest.

The Goodnight (21:00) now ends on the Night loop's first state (heavy eyes, dim warm breath, Bramble asleep) instead of black, and the Christmas Eve goodnight ends with everyone asleep instead of fading out, so each hands straight over to its night loop. The New Year's Day "Goodnight Season" still ends dark: no night loop after the season's last goodnight.

Status (24 Oct 2026)

Built: skits with ElevenLabs voices (tools/skit.py), skit arrangements, the silent loops (Waiting, Night, Morning, 25 Oct 2026), FPP playlists and schedule per site (tools/gen_site_config.py), and one ready-to-copy bundle per player with the night's real running times (tools/fpp_bundle.py → show-plan.md).

Still to do: the first run on a real FPP player (fpp/README.md "Not verified"), then HA (M7).

Show plan

Generated by python -m tools.fpp_bundle from the FPP playlists and schedule (tools/gen_site_config.py) and the rendered sequences; don't edit, change those and re-run. Every site plays the same nights; only its trees differ.

Season: 2026-12-01 to 2027-01-01. Priority when two overlap (fpp/README.md): the countdown, then goodnights, shows, announcements, the Night loop, and the waiting loop, which comes back by itself after each. The Night loop runs from the Goodnight until Home Assistant's lights out, or the end of its window at the latest; either way it stops gracefully: the piece playing ends, then Lights Out. The Morning loop isn't scheduled: Home Assistant starts it.

What's on: the Stair Tree Choir

Generated by python -m tools.fpp_bundle from the show schedule (tools/whats_on.py), like show-plan.md; don't edit it, change the schedule and re-run.

To copy and paste

The Stair Tree Choir is back! Six singing Christmas trees, every evening from 1 December to 1 January (to confirm). Lights on at 4pm, shows at 5, 6, 7 and 8pm (about 11-14 minutes), goodnight at 9pm.
Saturday Specials at 6pm with every song, a midnight countdown on New Year's Eve, and New Year's Day shows from 3pm. Bring your friends (and your grandma)!

A normal night

When What's happening
4pm Lights on. Between shows the trees muck about: waves, winks, games of catch, and Bramble nodding off. Every quarter of an hour they tell you when the next show is.
5pm, 6pm, 7pm and 8pm Shows, about 11-14 minutes each: four songs, plus jokes and chat in between.
9pm Goodnight: the choir says goodnight and settles down.
after 9pm The trees doze, yawn and giggle quietly, with the lights turned down low. Lights out by 11:30pm.

The trees also wake up with us in the mornings: yawning, stretching and watching everyone go off to work and school.

What's in each show

Three different shows, so if you stay for more than one you'll see something new.

Show Songs
The 5 and 8 o'clock show Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree, Dominick the Donkey, Little Drummer Boy, We Wish You a Merry Christmas
The 6 o'clock show Feliz Navidad, Frosty the Snowman, O Come All Ye Faithful, Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree
The 7 o'clock show We Wish You a Merry Christmas, Twelve Days of Christmas, The Virgin Mary Had a Baby Boy, Dominick the Donkey

Special nights

Date What's different
Saturdays 5, 12, 19 and 26 December At 5pm a short taster (two songs), then at 6pm the Saturday Special: every Christmas song we know in one go (about 28 minutes). The other shows as normal.
Wednesday 23 December: Village Night The big one. At 6pm the Village Special with every song; the 5pm and 7pm shows have auditions for new voices from the crowd.
Thursday 24 December: Christmas Eve Santa phones in during every show. At 9pm the choir falls asleep one by one so he can come, and they stay asleep all night.
Thursday 31 December: New Year's Eve Shows at 5pm, 6pm, 7pm, 8pm and 10pm, a late show at 11:15pm (Bramble swears he'll stay up), then the midnight countdown and Auld Lang Syne. Lights out by 12:30am.
Friday 1 January: New Year's Day New Year shows every hour from 3pm to 7pm: Happy New Year, Here Comes the Sun, Walking on Sunshine, What a Wonderful World, Auld Lang Syne. Then the choir says goodbye for the year at 7:30pm.

Meet the choir

Left to right: Holly (the conductor, bossy), Ivy (agrees with Holly), Noel (the tenor, holds every note too long), Jingle (very excited), Bramble (very sleepy) and Pip (the smallest, terrible jokes). More about them: backstory.md.

Still to confirm

  • The season dates (1 December to 1 January) are a placeholder until Rob confirms them.

Specials: Saturday Special, New Year's Eve, New Year's Day

Plan, 24 Oct 2026, from Rob's answers. Built the same evening: every skit, song and playlist below is rendered, render-checked and in the generator (tools/gen_site_config.py), and the real night-by-night times are in show-plan.md. Changes made while building: Saturday's 17:00 show is a two-song teaser ending "Save your voices!" so the special stays special; the NYE countdown playlist starts at 23:59:20 and says "Ten!" at 23:59:50; the New Year's Day show plays all five New Year songs (Happy New Year, Here Comes the Sun, Walking on Sunshine, What a Wonderful World, Auld Lang Syne). The normal night is in show-night.md.

The season with specials

Dates (2026–27) Night
1–30 Dec, Sun–Fri Normal night (show-night.md)
Sat 5, 12, 19, 26 Dec Normal night, but 18:00 is the Saturday Special
Thu 31 Dec New Year's Eve: normal shows, then late shows and the midnight countdown
Fri 1 Jan New Year's Day: New Year shows 15:00–19:00

The season's last date moves from 31 Dec to 1 Jan 2027.

Saturday Special (18:00, every December Saturday)

Every song in one block, instead of the usual 18:00 show (Set B). The 17:00, 19:00 and 20:00 shows stay as normal.

Proposed running order, about 29 minutes. All nine songs run 26:16 together, plus skits and 4 s pauses:

Piece
Special intro (new skit): Holly: "Welcome to the Saturday Special! Every song we know!" Jingle: "EVERY song?!" Ivy: "Especially that one."
1 Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree
2 Feliz Navidad
3 Dominick the Donkey
4 Frosty the Snowman
Bramble falls asleep
5 Little Drummer Boy (Bramble asleep)
6 Twelve Days of Christmas (still asleep)
Bramble wakes up (special) (new skit): "He slept through TWO songs!" "I was resting my eyes. Twice."
7 O Come All Ye Faithful
8 The Virgin Mary Had a Baby Boy
9 We Wish You a Merry Christmas
Thank you (special) (new skit)

Bramble's arc carries over: both "sleepy" songs sit between him falling asleep and waking. The set-list test should allow two in a row.

Announcing it ("that day and the week before"):

When What changes
Saturday, 16:15–16:45 Announcements say "next show at five, and at six it's the Saturday Special!" (new: announce-17-sat)
Saturday, 17:15–17:45 "The Saturday Special starts at six: every song!" (new: announce-special, replacing announce-18)
Saturday, 17:00 show Its thank-you plugs the special at six (new: thank-you-sat)
Sun–Fri, up to 25 Dec Every show's thank-you adds "and this Saturday at six: the Saturday Special!" (new: thank-you-week)
27–30 Dec Thank-yous plug New Year's Eve instead: "We're staying up till midnight!" (new: thank-you-nye)

The Show A/B/C playlists therefore come in thank-you variants (normal, Saturday, week, NYE), generated rather than hand-made.

New Year's Eve (Thu 31 Dec): to the midnight countdown

Time What plays
16:00–23:58 Waiting loop, with announcements as usual (the 19:xx ones announce "more shows later tonight")
17:00, 18:00, 19:00, 20:00 Normal shows (Sets A, B, C, A), thank-you plugs "see you at midnight!"
22:00 Set B
23:15 NYE show: new skit Bramble's staying up. Holly: "Bramble's going to stay awake until midnight." Bramble: "Easy." Then two or three songs. Bramble nods off during the last one.
23:59:00 Countdown (highest priority): 50 s of build-up, everyone counting 10…1 from 23:59:50, "Happy New Year!" at 00:00:00, and Bramble waking on the bang. Then Auld Lang Syne, with Noel holding the last "syyyyne".
about 00:06 Goodnight (New Year): "See you next year!", then the Night loop until lights out, 00:30 at the latest. No 21:00 goodnight that night.

Things to get right:

  • The clock. FPP starts the countdown on its own clock, so the Pi needs internet time that night. At home the site router's WAN can plug into the home network. Check the time on FPP's Status page before 23:00. If the clock might be off, the countdown is the only thing that would be wrong.
  • An entry crossing midnight (23:59 start, 00:09 end): check that FPP 10.3 handles an end time earlier than the start time on the bench. If not, split it at 23:59:59.
  • Volume after 23:00. Neighbours. A quieter level for the late shows, or a word with them beforehand.

New Year's Day (Fri 1 Jan): afternoon into evening

Shows at 15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00 and 19:00 (sunset is about 16:05, so most run in the dark), the waiting loop in between, then a "see you next Christmas" goodnight at about 19:30.

New Year music: one set of about 4 songs (around 12 minutes), no Christmas songs. Rob picks the songs and supplies the MP3s. Suggestions that would lip-sync well:

Song Why
Auld Lang Syne Shared with the midnight countdown, so it's built once
Happy New Year (ABBA) The obvious one, slow and clear for mouths
Celebration (Kool & the Gang) Big chorus for the whole choir
What a Wonderful World Gentle; Bramble manages to stay awake for it
Walking on Sunshine / Here Comes the Sun Bright for a January afternoon

New skits: New Year intro (Pip's New Year joke; Bramble: "Is it still Christmas?"), thank-you (New Year), and goodnight (season): "See you next Christmas!"

Building it

New pieces:

  • Skits: special intro, Bramble wakes (special), thank-you variants (sat, week, nye, special, New Year), announce-17-sat, announce-special, Bramble's staying up, the countdown, goodnight (New Year), New Year intro, goodnight (season). About 15 short scripts; the ElevenLabs cost is small, under 3,000 characters.
  • Songs: Auld Lang Syne, plus 3–4 New Year songs, each going through the per-song checklist (lyric timing, beats, sequence, arrangement, render check).
  • Countdown sequence: lights and a choir-wide burst on the stroke of midnight, with the countdown voices.
  • Generator (tools/gen_site_config.py): Saturday-only entries (day 6) and the normal 18:00 show on Sun–Fri (FPP day mask 0x17E00 = INX_DAY_MASK + every day but Saturday; constants from FPP 10.3 src/ScheduleEntry.h), dated entries for 31 Dec and 1 Jan, playlist variants, the season extended to 1 Jan, and tests for the priority and dates.
  • show-plan.md will then list each kind of night.

Order, given 1 Dec is the deadline for the six trees: Saturday Special first (the first one is Sat 5 Dec), then New Year's Eve, then New Year's Day (the music needs Rob's picks first).

Village Night (Wed 23 Dec) and Christmas Eve (Thu 24 Dec)

Added 24 Oct 2026 (Rob: "the 23rd lots of people in the village congregate, as many travel to family Christmas Eve"). Both use guest voices: the audition voices nobody was cast as (data/voices.json "guests"). A guest has no tree, so no mouth moves; every tree looks where the voice comes from instead: down at the crowd, up at the sky, or at Holly when the call comes through her "phone".

Guest Voice Where the trees look
Santa George up (the sleigh radio)
Dame Matilda (opera) Matilda down (in the crowd)
One-Note Callum Callum down
Big Adam (shower singer) Adam down
Little Jess (aged seven) Jessica down
Cousin Charlie (Sydney) Charlie Holly (on the phone)
Uncle Brian (wants a mince pie) Brian Holly

Village Night, 23 Dec: the busiest night of the year.

Time What plays
16:15–16:45 "Next show at five, and at six the Village Special!" (announce-17-village)
17:00 Set A with Choir Auditions after the tuning-up: hopefuls for a seventh tree "next Christmas" (a wink at the extra trees); the thank-you says "don't go, at six it's the Village Special"
17:15–17:45 announce-village-special
18:00 Village Special: every song, the Saturday Special's running order, opening with the roll-call: relatives ring Holly's phone (a cousin in Sydney, Little Jess's message for her nan in the bobble hat, Uncle Brian's mince pie)
19:00 Set C with the auditions; thank-you: "off to family tomorrow? Safe travels! Staying? Santa might ring tomorrow!"
20:00 Set A with the roll-call

From Sun 20 Dec the weekday thank-yous plug "Wednesday at six, the Village Special" (thank-you-vil-week); before that they plug the Saturday Special as usual.

Christmas Eve, 24 Dec: a normal night's times. Santa rings the sleigh radio in every show (santa-calls: Bramble says he'll stay up to see him; Santa only comes when everyone's asleep). At 20:00 he's over the rooftops (santa-nearly). Thank-yous: leave a carrot for the reindeer. At 21:00 Goodnight Christmas Eve: the trees fall asleep one by one (Bramble first, Holly last), eyes shut and outlines breathing, and stay asleep: the Night Christmas Eve loop (everyone asleep, only the gentlest stirring) runs until lights out, then they fade out one by one (25 Oct 2026; it used to fade to dark straight away).

ElevenLabs: about 2,800 characters for all 13 skits, nearly all that was left on the plan in October; lines two skits share are cached and paid for once.

← What's on: the Stair Tree ChoirThe Stair Tree Choir: who they are →

The Stair Tree Choir: who they are

For anyone running a show night, and for the name tags. The six characters are in show-night.md; everything here matches what they say and do in the skits.

How the choir began (the 20-second version)

For years they were a spiral staircase. Oak steps, going round and round, up and down, every single day. Every time someone ran up them, they creaked, and every time someone tiptoed down at night, they creaked a bit quieter. That's a lot of practice.

When the staircase was taken out, the steps refused to be firewood. "We've been singing for years," said the top step. "Nobody noticed." So they became trees, grew some lights, and started a choir.

Every step became a tree. Six voices, because, as Holly says, "Not everyone needs to sing at once, Jingle."

The six

Left to right as you face them. At a site with fewer trees, the first ones along are the ones you meet: Holly is always on the left.

1. Holly: the conductor

Name tag: Holly · Conductor · "Places, everyone!"

Holly was the top step. She spent years looking down on everyone and saw no reason to stop. She counts every song in, keeps everyone in time, and sighs a lot. She secretly loves it when the audience claps, and pretends not to.

  • Catchphrase: "Places, everyone! Places!"
  • Can't stand: Noel's long notes. Bramble's naps. Jingle's questions. (She loves them all really.)
  • If you ask her anything: "Not now, we're about to start."

2. Ivy: the sidekick

Name tag: Ivy · Assistant Conductor · "Especially you."

Ivy was the step just below Holly, which is where she's been ever since: one step behind, agreeing. Holly and Ivy have been together longer than anyone can remember. Ivy is the one who notices when Bramble has dozed off, and is quietly the funniest tree in the choir.

  • Catchphrase: "Especially you."
  • Favourite job: whispering "He was asleep again."
  • Secret: she knows all of Holly's words before Holly says them.

3. Noel: the tenor

Name tag: Noel · Tenor (he'll tell you) · "Miiiiiii!"

Noel was the creaky step in the middle, the one you could hear from every room. He has always thought of it as singing. He warms up before every show, holds every last note for far too long, and has been told "THANK you, Noel" more times than any tree in history.

  • Catchphrase: "Mi mi mi mi miiiiiii!"
  • Best moment: the end of "Goodniiiiiight!"
  • Ambition: a solo. Holly says no.

4. Jingle: the excitable one

Name tag: Jingle · Enthusiast · "Can I? Can I?"

Jingle was the step that squeaked when children ran up the stairs, so he's been excited his whole life. He talks fast, asks to sing every song, and still can't believe he gets to be in a choir. Every single show is the best show ever.

  • Catchphrase: "Ooh, ooh, can I sing the next one?"
  • Favourite word: "Again!"
  • Covers for Bramble on the fifth day of Christmas, every time, with Pip.

5. Bramble: the sleepy one

Name tag: Bramble · Bass, mostly asleep · "I was resting my eyes."

Bramble was the bottom step. For years everyone sat on him to put their boots on, so he's very, very tired. He means to stay awake, honestly, but one gentle song and he's off. When he's asleep his eyes close and his lights go slow and blue, breathing in and out. Watch for it.

  • Catchphrase: "I was resting my eyes."
  • Has slept through: Little Drummer Boy (the "pa rum pum pum pum" is a lullaby to him) and the whole of the Twelve Days of Christmas, including his own verse.
  • Wakes up to: Holly shouting "Bramble!" He always answers "Present!"

6. Pip: the joker

Name tag: Pip · Smallest voice · Terrible jokes

Pip was the little step at the turn of the spiral, the one everyone forgot was there until they tripped on it. So Pip makes sure nobody forgets now: big jokes from the smallest voice. The jokes are awful and Pip knows it, which is the point.

  • Catchphrase: "What do you call a tree that's afraid of Christmas? A fir-raidy cat!"
  • Wants everyone to come back and bring their grandma (and their grandma's friends).
  • Last word of the night: "Don't let the reindeer bite!"

If someone asks

They ask You say
Are they real wood? Yes, solid oak: they were the steps of a spiral staircase.
How do they sing? Each tree has 92 lights and its own little computer on the back. A player in the box sends every tree its lights and plays the voices through the speaker.
Who's who? Holly's on the left; then Ivy, Noel, Jingle, Bramble, Pip.
Why is that one blue? That's Bramble. He's asleep. Holly will wake him up in a minute.
When's the next show? The trees announce it every quarter of an hour. Shows are at 5, 6, 7 and 8.
Can I touch them? Please don't: they're plugged in, and Bramble's a light sleeper.

Show webcam

A camera in the farmer's hedge across the road streams the Site A shows live to the village, family and friends. The same footage is also cut into clips to post afterwards. This is separate from the tree build and not needed for 1 Dec. This page holds the scope and BOM; nothing is built yet (24 Oct 2026).

Scope

  • Live: the shows only, from about 5 minutes before each show to a minute or two after. That's 17:00, 18:00, 19:00 and 20:00 (11–14 min each), plus the specials in specials.md: Saturday 18:00, NYE countdown, NYD. The waiting loop and announcements between shows are not streamed.
  • Clips: every show is recorded with full, unmuted audio. Clips per song and per skit are posted afterwards (see Clips).

Constraints

  • The hedge is about 20 m from the house with a clear view. It has no power and no WiFi, and it belongs to the farmer.
  • The internet is the Huawei B818 4G hub, with unlimited data.
  • Budget about £150–200. An earlier draft with a point-to-point link and a 100 Ah battery came to £560+ and was turned down.

Design

[hedge]  WiFi camera (12V) <- MOSFET <- ESP32 (deep sleep) <- 3A fuse <- 12V 20Ah LiFePO4   (one box at the foot of a stake)
             ~~~ 2.4 GHz WiFi, ~20 m open air ~~~
[garden] Site A Cudy WR3000 (outdoors at the site box) -> home LAN
         Site A Pi 5 (FPP; see the note below): ffmpeg takes the camera's RTSP feed (video copied) + FPP's own audio
                            -> YouTube Live (auto-muted, see below)  and  -> local recording (full audio)

Network. No bridge is needed. The Site A router is already outdoors in the front garden, so the camera joins its WiFi across about 20 m of open air. If the signal at the hedge is weak, a directional antenna on the Cudy (about £10) fixes it.

Camera. A cheap outdoor WiFi camera, for example a Tapo C320WS/C325WB (ColorPro, good in the dark) or a Reolink RLC-510WA. Before ordering, check that it:

  • has RTSP output
  • runs on 12V DC
  • can switch IR off (otherwise the hedge leaves flare)
  • lets you lower the exposure if possible (otherwise the pixels blow out)

At 20 m, a fixed lens of about 4–6 mm frames the house front, so no zoom is needed. Turn the camera mic off. The stream takes clean sound from FPP, and passers-by aren't recorded.

Power control: ESP32 with deep sleep

An ESPHome ESP32 switches the camera through a logic-level MOSFET and measures the battery through a voltage divider. It is one of the spare DevKitC-32U boards (10 bought, 6 needed for December), powered by a spare Mini560.

It sleeps between shows, which is what makes it better than a timer here:

  • It wakes about 6 minutes before each show and switches the camera on. The camera needs about a minute to boot and join WiFi.
  • While awake it syncs its clock, reports the battery voltage to HA, and fetches the next on/off times.
  • It switches the camera off a minute or two after the show ends, then deep-sleeps until the next wake.

Where the schedule comes from: it is generated from the FPP schedule (tools/gen_site_config.py), so the specials, NYE and NYD are included. It is baked into the ESPHome config as the default, and HA can override it on each wake (for example "skip tonight", or "on now").

Fail-safes:

  • Maximum on-time. A hard maximum on-time of 1 h per wake, except the NYE countdown, so a hung ESP or missed command can't drain the battery.
  • No WiFi. If WiFi is down on wake, it falls back to the baked-in schedule.
  • Manual override. A switch in the box bypasses the MOSFET for testing.

Power budget
Camera, IR off, ~4 W × ~1¾ h a night ~7 Wh
ESP32 awake while the camera is on, plus deep sleep (DevKitC regulator/USB chip and Mini560 idle, ~10 mA) ~1.5 Wh
Per night ~9 Wh
12V 20 Ah LiFePO4 256 Wh, ~200 Wh usable
Runtime ~3 weeks per charge, about 2 charges a season; charge it indoors at home

Saturday specials and the NYE countdown run longer; they add a few Wh each. No solar: December yield is poor, LiFePO4 must not charge below 0°C, and a panel on the hedge invites theft.

For comparison, a plain 12V timer can't follow the specials. With one window of about 16:50–20:20 it uses ~14 Wh a night (~2 weeks per charge), with no battery reading. An ESP32 that stays awake on WiFi uses ~17 Wh a night.

Stream and recording

  • Note (Rob, 26 Oct 2026): Site A's player is now the Pi 3, which is too slow to relay as well. Before the webcam goes ahead: either swap the Pi 5 back in as the Site A player, or run the relay on the Pi 5 beside it with FPP's audio sent across the network. Undecided.
  • Relay process. ffmpeg runs on the Site A Pi 5 at low priority (nice) and copies the video, so the Pi never transcodes. Audio comes from FPP's own output through an ALSA loopback and is encoded to AAC. A one-off -itsoffset cancels the camera's ~1–2 s delay.
  • Start and stop. The relay starts at the camera's on-time and stops after each show, following the same schedule as the ESP32.
  • Live. The stream goes to YouTube Live with one persistent stream key and auto-start/stop, so each show becomes its own live video. The channel's /live link always points at whichever is on, so one link serves the whole season for family and the village Facebook group. About 720p–1080p at 2.5–4 Mbps, roughly 4 GB a night.
  • Recording. The same ffmpeg also writes each show to disk with the unmuted audio, about 2 GB per show, on a USB stick on the Pi. They're copied to the PC each night.
  • Fallback. If the relay ever disturbs FPP timing, move it to a separate Pi with one of the spare USB sound cards on a split of the amp input.

Clips

FPP knows when each sequence starts and ends. A small tool (to write) reads that log and cuts each night's recording into one clip per song and per skit, named after the sequence. Picking the best ones to post is a manual job.

Where to post:

  • YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok using the app's own licensed music library: post the clip with the song added from the app, lined up with the trees by hand. That's the legitimate way to post the commercial songs. Which songs are in each library varies.
  • Ordinary YouTube uploads with the original audio: copyrighted songs usually get claimed (the rights holder takes the ads), not blocked or given a strike. That's far more forgiving than live.
  • Skits, Auld Lang Syne and any public-domain carols: post as-is, with no music issue.

Music copyright

YouTube Content ID (and Facebook's Rights Manager) matches recordings. A carol that is out of copyright still gets flagged if the recording is a modern one. A match on a live stream can mute it, replace it with a placeholder, or cut it off, and repeated matches can lead to a strike. The camera mic would pick up the songs too, so camera audio doesn't avoid this. Streaming only the shows doesn't help either: the shows are where the commercial songs play.

The ID3 tags on the show MP3s (Documents\xLights\Audio\Songs) sort them like this:

Risk Songs Why
Low Auld Lang Syne From archive.org (a public-domain folk-song collection)
Medium O Come All Ye Faithful, The Virgin Mary Had a Baby Boy, Twelve Days of Christmas, We Wish You a Merry Christmas The songs are traditional, but these are 2017 compilation recordings ("Christmas Carol"). Those are often registered with Content ID.
High Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree, Dominick the Donkey, Feliz Navidad, Little Drummer Boy, What a Wonderful World, Happy New Year, Here Comes the Sun, Walking on Sunshine, Frosty the Snowman Major-label recordings, and the songs themselves are under copyright

Live plan: always stream the video; stream the sound only when it is safe.

  • The relay mutes the live audio (an ffmpeg volume filter) whenever FPP is playing a track on a "muted" list. FPP's current sequence is available from its API or via Node-RED.
  • The recording keeps the full audio for clips.
  • Skits stay audible.
  • During a muted song the trees perform in silence, and the stream title says "come and hear it on the street".
  • Swap the medium-risk carols for public-domain or CC0 recordings (Musopen, archive.org, or a home recording) so they can be heard live too. They then need re-timing with tools/lyric_timing.py / tools/xl_timing.py.
  • If even the muted stream gets flagged, fall back to video only.

Playing on the street (separate from the stream). In the UK, playing recorded music in public technically needs a PPL PRS licence (TheMusicLicence). That licence is aimed at businesses and organisations. A free display at a private home is a grey area, and enforcement against one is unheard of. Two things would change that:

  • Donations: collecting donations, even for charity, makes it look like an event. Ask PPL PRS first.
  • YouTube rips: several MP3s look like YouTube rips (Happy New Year, Here Comes the Sun, Walking on Sunshine). Buying them as downloads makes the sources clean.

Open question: a short email to PPL PRS describing the display would settle it. None of this is legal advice.

Checks before buying

  1. Copyright test. Rob requested live streaming on 24 Oct 2026; it can take up to 24 h to switch on. tools/stream_test.py runs the test from the PC; the steps are below. Note what gets flagged.
  2. The farmer. Get permission, ideally in writing, and ask when they flail the hedge (cutting season is Sept–Feb). Check whether the hedge or verge is highway land.
  3. Privacy. A camera that publishes the road falls outside the domestic CCTV exemption, so:
    • frame the house and trees
    • privacy-mask the road and pavement in the camera
    • keep camera audio off
    • stream only at show times
  4. WiFi at the hedge. Stand at the hedge with a phone and check the signal from the router that will serve the camera. Until the Cudy is in place, use the Zyxel's 2.4 GHz.
  5. 4G upload at show times on a few evenings: at least 4 Mbps for 720p, or 6 Mbps for 1080p.

Running the copyright test

python -m tools.stream_test build renders previews/stream-test.mp4: the trees singing Rockin' (high risk), O Come All Ye Faithful (medium) and Auld Lang Syne (low), back to back, about 9 minutes at 720p. Add song names (data/songs/<name>.json) to test others, or --seconds 20 for a quick one.

  1. Set up the broadcast. In YouTube Studio go to Create → Go live → Stream. Set visibility to Unlisted, made for kids No, and leave DVR on.
  2. Store the stream key. Copy the key into a user environment variable called YT_STREAM_KEY. Set it the same way as FPP_PASSWORD, and never put it in git.
  3. Push the video. Run .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m tools.stream_test stream. It sends the file in real time, so it takes as long as the video.
  4. Watch and record what happens. Watch the Studio preview and the stream's Copyright notices during and after the run. For each song, note whether it played, was muted, was replaced, or the stream was stopped. Write the results here, and the auto-mute list comes from that.

Phases

  • S0: the checks above.
  • S1, bench:
    • ESPHome config: deep-sleep schedule, MOSFET, battery sensor, fail-safes.
    • Real draw: measure it awake, asleep and with the camera on.
    • Relay: the relay on the Pi 5, with auto-mute and recording, for a 1-hour unlisted soak.
    • Exposure: set it against a lit tree.
  • S2, install before 1 Dec: stake, box, aim and focus at dusk, privacy masks.
  • S3, clips tool: cut recordings per sequence from FPP's log.
  • S4, Home Assistant (in the HA repo, optional):
    • a camera entity and a hall board tile
    • a battery level and low-battery alert
    • skip/on-now overrides for the ESP32

Design review, 1 Nov 2026

A review of the tree design from the source, the data and the WLED and FPP code. Nothing here has been changed in the design: every item is Rob's to decide. Nothing was tested on hardware, and the OpenSCAD solids weren't rendered, so the sizes are worked out from the parameters. Figures marked "estimate" are engineering estimates.

Scope is December 2026: 6 trees at Site A.

The tree box moved to FreeCAD after this was written (enclosure/tree-box.FCStd, same geometry), so every item below still stands unless it is marked fixed. tree-box.scad line numbers refer to the frozen copy in feet/old-tree-box/.

Fix before the first show

Nothing to stand the trees on

The boots are parked and nothing replaces them. A finished tree is about 5kg (estimate) with its centre of area 356mm above the base, and on its own base it tips at about 3 m/s of wind. A gust of 20–30 m/s gives about 26–87 Nm at the base (estimate), which weight alone can't resist. It needs a staked post or similar, designed for about 130 Nm. Standoffs on the back have to miss pixels 64, 71 and 77 at x = 191. The bottom edge also needs keeping off the grass.

This sits at the top because it holds up other items: the build guide's stage 7 and final assembly steps, the bottom-edge height, and possibly the box position.

Tree box has no position

Nothing fixes where the box goes (gen_printed.py says "not placed yet"; wiring.html says "low down"). With 6mm of margin for the leads there are two windows:

  • Between the eyes and the lip (recommended): the plate's x = 0 edge at tree x 113–182, centred at about 147, cover bottom at y 600–640 from the top. Screws clear pixels by 36mm or more, no pixel leads cross it, and it is hidden from the front. The pixel lead to node 1 is about 310mm.
  • Low band: x 73–222, cover bottom at y ≈ 858, with only about 3mm of vertical play, and the antenna tip reaches 88mm below the tree.

WLED config (tools/gen_site_config.py:262)

Both come from the WLED 16.0.1 source and the generated config; neither has been seen on a real tree. Trees 1–9 were flashed with this config, so they need it applied again.

  1. Idle trees go orange. The config doesn't set def.on, so WLED boots on, orange, at brightness 128. WLED leaves realtime 2.5 s after the last frame, and FPP stops sending once nothing is playing unless alwaysTransmit is set (the repo never sets it; its default wasn't checked). So expect an orange flash in the 4 s pauses, and orange trees after Lights Out, at about 0.6A each. Fix: add "def": {"on": false} and set alwaysTransmit, then bench it.
  2. The show runs at about half brightness. if.live.maxbri isn't set, so DDP frames are scaled by brightness 128. It also hides the problem below, because the current tests read low. Fix: "if": {"live": {"en": true, "maxbri": true}}, and do the current tests at 255.

Pixel current is unmeasured

The 0.3W (25mA) per pixel figure has no source in the repo, and the limiter, fuses and voltage drop all rest on it. Forum reports for Ray Wu 12V 12mm pixels range from 30mA to 60mA. At 50mA full white is 4.6A, and because the limiter believes 25mA it would allow about 3.9A, over the 3A fuse. At brightness 128 that same tree reads about 2.3A, exactly what the test expects. Fix: measure one pixel at 255 with the limiter off, then set LED_MA and recheck the cap and the fuse. If 25mA holds, the arithmetic is fine: the limit lands at about 1.93A.

Mains

  • The test checklist has no check before first mains for the S-400-12's 230V switch, plug earth to case continuity, or L and N. They appear only in the build guide and wiring.html. The switch is a one-shot PSU killer.
  • The BOM has no cord grip, and no forks or ferrules for the PSU's screw terminals, and the grip in wiring.html is on a plate that isn't designed. A pulled lead could put live on the 12V wiring. Add an anchored lead with crimped ends and the earth longest.
  • CLAUDE.md §7 bans mains in a printed enclosure, while §4 puts the terminals under a printed hood that is open underneath with unverified sizes. Either state the exception or use a bought shroud.

Fix on the next tree box print

Item Evidence Fix
Mounting slots run the wrong way tree-box.scad:233 slots are vertical, along the grain, which barely moves. Oak moves across the grain, about 1–3mm over the 102mm screw span (estimate), against ±0.3 of play Horizontal slots on one column
M3 × 10 bottoms out Fixed 1 Nov 2026: the insert's hole now goes through the boss, so the M3 × 10 stays Done
Ears barely clear washers ear_w predates the wrap: a Ø9 washer clears the cover by 0.35mm Widen the ears 3mm
Coupon doesn't match the base The coupon prints the holes vertical, the base prints them horizontal Print the coupon on edge
No home for the Wagos No retention feature. The modelled ports sit 1mm from the SP16 and 1.5mm from each other Stack or turn them, with 20mm of wire room
No strain relief on the SP17 100N at 65mm is 6.5 Nm into a 3.5mm shelf with the layers across the load Clip the flex to the post

Check when the parts are in hand

  • Pixel leads: the 59→60 and 80→81 jumps are 195mm and 224mm, and the leads are probably 76–102mm. Plan two splices. About 4.7m of slack has no way of being held.
  • Pixel disk chamfer: pixel-disk.scad:52 chamfers the lip's back edge, where the clips grip. The test strip should show whether the clips still seat, or whether it needs removing to keep the full 2mm land.
  • Glue: cnc-cutting.md:66 has hot glue on oiled wood, and the hole grows 0.2–0.6mm across the grain. Exterior PU or MS in bare counterbores, before oiling, is safer.
  • Old finish: the photos look lacquered, with residue bands at both ends, so oil may not soak in. Confirm the species and strip first. Seal the end grain harder than oil, especially by the 12 bottom holes and node 36, 12.5mm from it.
  • Cover screw: the cord force is about 200–480N through one M3 (estimate), so expect creep in the PETG under the head. Leave the seal test loaded for a few days.
  • First controller board: the checklist catches the 5V move but not a leftover GND wire on F13 (now 3V3) or data on Q13 (now IO14). Meter F13, X3 and Q13 before fitting the ESP32.
  • Board shorts: L14–L15 (data) sits beside M14–M15 (GND), so meter it. README step 2 also fills the U1 and ESP32 holes with solder before the parts go in.
  • Player fuse: the Pi (about 1.2A) plus the amp at clipping (about 1.7A, estimate) nears the 3A fuse, and a blown fuse stops the show. Give the amp its own way.
  • Site box: heat looks fine in December (about 20K rise, estimate). Condensation on the IP20 mesh PSU at ground level is the bigger worry, so mount it high. Check the DRiBOX seals take all 10 cables.
  • Mini560 EN pad: reports conflict on whether it may float. S-400-12 inrush against the 3A plug fuse: no datasheet found. Bench both.
  • RP-SMA: the model has the nut inside, but many pigtails take it outside. It sets the recess.
  • Clip flare: a clearance above about Ø16 leaves too little disk wall.
  • Pilot holes for the 4 × 40 screws aren't documented: 2.5–3mm × 22mm.

Looks fine

  • Schematic: the 74AHCT125 pins, /OE, spare ties, R1, R2, C1, C2 and GPIO16. Netlist, drawing and connections.md agree, and regenerating gives byte-identical files.
  • Power: S-400-12 capacity, 11.5V at the tree, 0.75mm² on a 3A fuse if 25mA holds, the Wago 0V split, and the data ground. The limiter does apply to DDP.
  • Oak: 5.4mm minimum web between counterbores (9.4mm between holes), and 4.9mm from clearance holes to the old holes. Nothing loads them, and 45% holes at the lip row is still only about 1.4 MPa at 30 m/s.
  • Wood screws: 24mm of bite and 6mm of front skin.
  • Tree box: the roof and drip path, tool access for the rear nuts and the 45° screw, and the 2.4mm Mini560 clearance (the swing moves away from it). Params, scad and DIMS agree on the fittings. Pixel holes drain out of the back.

NX

cad/ held three old imports of the tree box and none of them was current, including the set that commit 0707947 calls wrap-round: it's the clip-on cover from 30 Oct. All three are now in archive/. Import cad/tree-box-assembly.step to see the real design; with the old names gone, NX should keep the plain part names.
